title: Global generation of algebra modules on an affine open
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative O_S-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], U an affine open, and M a module sheaf over A restricted to the slice site over U [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If restriction of scalars of M along O_S|U -> A|U is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], then M admits global generating sections (an epimorphism from a coproduct of copies of A|U). No quasi-coherence hypothesis on A and no relation generators are required.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph; EGA I, Proposition 9.6.1

proof.text: Transport the underlying quasi-coherent module from the slice over U to U.toScheme by overEquiv. Quasi-coherence is preserved by the continuous, cocontinuous site equivalence: apply the existing public Mathlib theorem isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isLeftAdjoint directly in the slice-generation proof (without a separate slice quasi-coherence declaration), using its unit-sheaf identification and continuity of Over.post. Identify the affine open subscheme with its spectrum and restrict along isoSpec.inv; this restriction preserves quasi-coherence.

For the resulting module N on Spec R, isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent identifies N with the tilde of its global sections. Mathlib presentationTilde for the set of all elements and all relations gives a presentation of that tilde. Transport along fromTildeΓ and take its generating sections. Map these generators along restriction by isoSpec.hom, then along the inverse slice equivalence. Colimit preservation and the unit-sheaf isomorphisms preserve generating families. The composite restriction is the identity by restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId, and the slice unit isomorphism returns the original underlying module.

Reuse the same generating sections for the algebra module. To prove that their A-linear evaluation is epi, let two A-linear maps agree after evaluation. The freeHomEquiv converts this into equality of the images of every generator. After restricting scalars the O-linear evaluations of the two maps agree, again by freeHomEquiv. Cancel the generating O-linear evaluation epimorphism. Equality of the scalar-restricted maps gives equality of the original maps objectwise, since restriction of scalars leaves their functions unchanged. This argument requires no quasi-coherence of A.

proof_origin.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph; EGA I, Proposition 9.6.1. D2 formalization uses Mathlib presentationTilde, affine and slice transport, and an elementary cancellation proof for scalar extension of generating families.
